Summary Description: Dr. Mohammad Atiquzzaman is a leading researcher at the intersection of federated learning, 6G-enabled wireless networks, and intelligent autonomous systems. His work spans privacy-preserving distributed ML, security of FL in vehicular and IoT networks, and the deployment of energy-aware, RIS-assisted UAV/UGV architectures for disaster response and smart-city applications. Notable contributions include unlearning-centric frameworks such as UaaS-SFL and DT-FU that enable post-compromise mitigation without full retraining, as well as MARL-based joint control of UAV trajectories and RIS configurations (DIRECT, MAPPO/PPO) for robust, low-latency, energy-efficient communication. He also explores privacy guarantees (γ-AdvNoise), robust initialization via median aggregation, and calibration-aware early stopping to prevent over-unlearning. Across these works, he demonstrates a strong emphasis on scalable, real-world-aligned solutions that fuse ML security, wireless communications, energy management, and autonomous aerial-ground coordination in 6G-era networks.
